accounting_date: The local calendar date, in the company timezone above, of the source document: invoice.issued_at for invoices, payment.timestamp for payments.

reporting_period.rule: A posting belongs to this period if and only if the accounting date of its source document falls between start and end inclusive. Ledger timestamps are stored in UTC.

fx.quote: 1 unit of source_currency = rate units of target_currency (the base currency).
fx.rate_date: Use the rate dated on the document's accounting date.
fx.settlement: AP is cleared at the invoice's rate; Bank is credited at the payment's rate; the difference is posted to account 7900.

rounding.rule: convert(amount_minor) = round_half_up(amount_minor / 10**exp(source) * rate, exp(target)) expressed in target minor units. Each document amount (or remittance line) is converted once, as a whole.

posting_rules.invoice: Dr expense / Cr 2000 AP, base amount of the invoice total.
posting_rules.payment_with_remittance: One Dr 2000 AP row per remittance line (invoice_id set) at the invoice's rate; Cr 1000 Bank at the payment's rate; difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_without_remittance: Dr 2090 Suspense / Cr 1000 Bank at the payment's rate. This is correct treatment.
posting_rules.reversal: Mirror image of the original invoice rows; an invoice reversed in full has no net effect.

allocation: Every remittance line (invoice_refs) of a payment must be applied in full to the referenced invoice's AP. Suspense is only for payments without remittance information.
duplicates: A supplier invoice is identified by (entity_id, vendor_ref). It may be recorded at most once, net of reversals. Equal amounts or equal vendor_ref across different suppliers are not duplicates.
